description: The single source of truth for what a pair file contains. Consumed through the generated header AnalysisScripts/GeneratedPairObjectContract.h by the pair-directory allowlist, the ten-block closure and the plotting-input validator, which previously held three divergent hand-maintained copies.

axes.presence: required = always written; conditional = written only under stated conditions, so absence is not an error.
axes.merge_semantics: additive_content = histogram/sparse summed bin-wise; additive_scalar = scalar summed; invariant = identical across inputs.
axes.closure: checked = the ten-block closure asserts central == sum of blocks; exempt = it does not, and closure_reason says why.
axes.since_schema: The earliest analysis schema whose files carry this object. Optional; defaults to the first entry of schema_versions. An object belongs to every schema from since_schema onward.
axes.identity_checked: true = the ten-block closure asserts the central file and all ten blocks carry an IDENTICAL value. Optional, defaults false. Distinct from closure, which asserts central == sum of blocks: an invariant has nothing to sum, but blocks disagreeing about a contract string means the sum is over objects that do not mean the same thing.

schema_versions_doc: The contract is exact-match in BOTH directions, so it has to know which schema a directory was written under: a contract that expects a v3 object would otherwise fail every correct v2 directory, and a v2 contract would reject a correct v3 one. Consumers select by the file's own analysis_schema string, mapped through schema_version_tags, and FAIL CLOSED on any tag not listed here rather than falling back to a default. Listed oldest first.

objects.name: hFlavourClosure
objects.closure_reason: Filled with Fill(closureValues, closureWeight) at analysis/status_analysis_THnSparse_qq.C:1008, so it is additive on the same footing as the other sparses. It was omitted from Validation/ValidatePairBlockClosure.C:266-268 when 7cf9f86 added it to the pair-file contract, so the ten-block closure silently skipped it: 1500 content checks over 300 files is 5 objects per file, not 6.

objects.name: hFlavourClosureSpecies
objects.closure_reason: The species-resolved parallel of hFlavourClosure: the same shape with the 6-bin heavyStateCategory axis replaced by the 202-bin species ordinal. Filled with Fill(values, weight) beside hFlavourClosure, so it is additive on the same footing as the other sparses and closes over the ten disjoint blocks identically. It is a NEW object rather than a widening of hFlavourClosure, which stays byte-identical: hFlavourClosure carried 124,494 filled bins at 100 inputs and is the object whose merge cost produced a 49x step whose mechanism is still unknown, so widening it in place could not be bounded. Present only from v3 -- a correct v2 directory does not carry it, which is why the object set is keyed on the file's declared analysis_schema.

objects.name: hFlavourClosureSummary
objects.closure_reason: Two independent reasons, both at analysis/status_analysis_THnSparse_qq.C:1124-1135. It is written only when trigger.weightedTriggers > 0, so it is absent from any pair file whose trigger produced no weight in that job -- requiring it would fail every rare species. And its three bins are populated with SetBinContent, not Fill, so it carries no meaningful Sumw2 and a content+Sumw2 comparison would not mean what it means for the sparses. Its bins are extensive sums and would close on content alone; add a content-only, presence-conditional check before treating this as verified.

objects.name: species_ordinal_schema
objects.closure_reason: Provenance or contract string, identical in every input. Exempt from the SUM closure because there is nothing to sum; it is nonetheless checked for identity across the central file and all ten blocks, because a block disagreeing about which ordinal table it used would make the species axis of the sum meaningless.

objects.name: species_ordinal_labels
objects.closure_reason: The F5 legibility object: the ordinal -> PDG map, so a reader can decode the 202-bin species axis without this repository. Invariant, and identity-checked across the central file and its ten blocks for the same reason as species_ordinal_schema -- two blocks filled against different ordinal tables would sum bins that do not mean the same thing.

objects.name: species_ordinal_digest
objects.closure_reason: FNV-1a over the canonical ordinal:pdg serialisation, identifying WHICH ordinal table filled the axis without requiring a reader to parse 202 label entries to find out. Invariant and identity-checked with the other two.
